notes: A mobile with AFF_WATERWALK enters SECT_WATER_SWIM through the live mobile_activity pulse. Source and destination observers compare the canonical leave/arrival acts; six equivalent exits expose the shared C number(0,18) door draw. The port reuses the has_boat predicate for water capability.

C walks the prepended character_list, so the newest mobile consumes its door and sound draws before an older scavenger consumes number(0,10). The real MobileActivity test pins the mixed per-mobile draw sequence; the unsequenced activeMobs map walk fails this proof (R1/R3/R5e/R5h).

A successful mobile wander calls perform_move, which runs mp_greet after entry_prog when the mover is not sneaking. A destination dog consumes number(0,5) before the wanderer's following sound gate; the focused activity test pins that order and output (R1/R3/R5e/R5h).

After the unconditional sound gate calls mp_sound, C reaches the demon and dog tails even when the mob vnum has no switch case. Tests pin the number(0,2) demon and number(0,25) dog draws and the demon alignment transition (R1/R3/R5e/R5h).

A mobile with AFF_FLY enters SECT_FLYING through the live mobile_activity pulse. The source observer compares the leave act and exposes the shared C number(0,18) door draw; C room_activity ejects the non-flying destination observer, so the flying arrival act is pinned by TestMobileActivityWanderActsMatchPerformMove. NPC PRF flags use C's dummy_mob preference record and do not grant flight.

A failed water/flying sector gate is C's outer-loop continue: after the door draw it skips sound's number(0,15), pulse scripts, aggression, race-hate, and the rest of this mob's dispatch. The real MobileActivity tests pin draw order, blocked movement, aggression suppression, waterwalk/fly/boat/immortal access, and waterwalk/boat exclusion from flying rooms.

The Go wander path uses the canonical Act output to match C's hidden-invisible delivery, sentence capitalization, sneak suppression, and direction-sensitive destination acts. The unit proof pins source/destination bytes and silent sneaking movement.

The real MobileActivity test rejects an invisible-only weaker NPC target at level 33 and accepts a visible weaker NPC while pinning pulse draws. The paired God/NOHASSLE oracle scenario passes at the reference build after the fixture clears the attacker's AFF_DETECT_INVIS and gives the target AFF_INVISIBLE; this also proves level alone does not reveal an invisible target (R1/R3/R5e/R5h).

C sends one of two room acts before the memory hit: the exclaim when can_speak, the growl otherwise, both inside one ROOM_PEACEFUL gate. The real-pulse test drives MobileActivity and pins the exact bytes for the speak arm, the silent arm (race 12 is outside intelligent_races[]) and the peaceful suppression, and the attack that follows. Reverting the acts makes it fail (R1/R4/R5h).

C sends act("$n jumps to the aid of $N!") for the first mobile it can see fighting a player, then hits that player. The real-pulse test pins the bytes and the combat pair, and its invisible-player case proves the CAN_SEE gate; both fail on revert (R1/R4/R5h).

A charmed helper whose master is fighting calls do_assist and ends its pulse. The mobile-side port drops the descriptor-less TO_CHAR lines and pins the helpee line, the room line and the swing; TestMobAssistGuards covers the already-fighting, mounted and no-opponent gates. Both fail on revert (R1/R4/R5h).

C selects the first visible non-NOHASSLE player of level 24+ and then emits the grin and the two-line can_speak pair before hit(). The real-pulse test pins all three lines in order and the combat pair; reverting the acts makes it fail (R1/R4/R5h).

C's hit() never calls set_fighting; damage() enrols the pair, and its peaceful arm is gated on FIGHTING(victim) != ch, so the FIRST swing in a ROOM_PEACEFUL room is refused and nothing is enrolled. The port's hit() equivalent (StartCombat) enrols first and the refusal runs later in the combat pulse, where C's own second-hit exemption applies, so the first hit lands. Found while building DP-1435's oracle fixtures (room 8162 is ROOM_PEACEFUL); the fixtures were withdrawn rather than fixed here. Evidence: docs/fidelity/depth/handoff/2026-10-14-dp1371-backlog-batch.md.

CAN_GO refuses an EX_CLOSED exit, so a wandering mob stays behind a closed door and moves again once it opens. The port implemented CAN_GO as "the exit exists" and mobs walked through closed and locked doors (DP-1428). The door state is read from the live room, as player movement does. R1/R5h.
